flawed_step: Step 2: Inferring P(|X_n-X|>eps)→0 from convergence of the marginal distribution functions is unjustified. Convergence in distribution does not control the coupling between X_n and X on their common probability space.
counterexample: Let Ω={-1,1}, with all subsets measurable and P({-1})=P({1})=1/2. Define X(ω)=ω and X_n(ω)=-ω for every n. Each X_n has exactly the same Rademacher distribution as X, so F_{X_n}(t)=F_X(t) for every t and hence X_n converges to X in distribution. However, |X_n(ω)-X(ω)|=2 for every ω. Taking eps=1 gives P(|X_n-X|>1)=1 for every n, which does not tend to 0. Thus X_n does not converge to X in probability.
assessment_summary: The premise provides only convergence of marginal laws, while convergence in probability depends on the joint relationship between X_n and X. The explicit sign-reversal coupling satisfies the premise but violates the conclusion.
